title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X = C/Λ, a complex torus (an elliptic curve). G is the group of holomorphic and antiholomorphic automorphisms of X fixing the origin. The antiholomorphic involutions σ (real structures) act on Λ as reflections of the plane.

For a reflection σ, put Λ+ = Ker(σ−1) and Λ− = Ker(σ+1), each of rank 1, with generators e+ and e−. There are two cases:
- Λ = Λ+ ⊕ Λ−. This is the rectangular case, family E_a, real locus with two components.
- Λ+ ⊕ Λ− has index 2 in Λ. This is the rhombic case, family E'_a, real locus with one component.
The invariant is a = a(σ) = Q(e−)/Q(e+), where Q is the quadratic (length) form. The page's marginal note says this works for both E_a and E'_a.

Top of page: Grothendieck sets himself the task of relating a to τ or to the real modular invariant j. He tentatively guesses j = c·log a, a guess he partly crosses out.

Main argument:
- −σ is the reflection in the line orthogonal to the axis of σ. Passing from σ to −σ swaps Λ+ and Λ−. Hence a(−σ) = 1/a(σ), valid in every case.
- Therefore a(−σ) = a(σ) ⟺ a = 1 ⟺ the square lattice.
- He compares conjugacy of σ and −σ in G, by lattice symmetry type n:
  - n = 2 (non-anharmonic case): Aut = {±1}, the anti-automorphisms are ±σ, and G = {±1, ±σ} is commutative. So −σ is not conjugate to σ. The two real structures are either both of type E (E_a and E_{1/a}) or both of type E' (E'_a and E'_{1/a}).
  - n = 6 (hexagonal case): −σ is not conjugate to σ (vertex reflections versus face reflections).
  - n = 4 (square case): −σ is conjugate to σ via rotation by i. This is the only case where that happens.
- The next page completes the classification:
  - square: types E_1 (axis reflections) and E'_1 (diagonal reflections);
  - hexagonal: E'_{√3} and E'_{1/√3};
  - otherwise: a pair {E_a, E_{1/a}} or {E'_a, E'_{1/a}} with a ≠ 1.

Purpose: a preliminary to the 'surgery of conformal surfaces' project. It classifies the real (anticonformal-involution) structures on conformal tori and their moduli.

This is the classical classification of real elliptic curves up to isomorphism: rectangular versus rhombic lattices, with the real j-line split at j = 1728.
errors: The guess j = c·log a is incorrect. j is a transcendental modular function of τ, with τ = i√a or i·a up to normalisation in the rectangular case. Only asymptotically does log j behave like 2π·(√a or a). The rectangular family covers j ≥ 1728 and the rhombic family covers j ≤ 1728 (normalised).

Possible inconsistency with the next page. If a = Q(e−)/Q(e+) with Q the squared length, then in the hexagonal case Q(2v−u)/Q(u) = 3, not √3. The value √3 is the ratio of lengths, not of squared lengths. Either Q denotes the length or a should be 3.
Minor point: in the n = 2 case, 'non conjugué' holds trivially because G is commutative. The text's 'bien non non conjugué' is a slip in the writing.

ideas.what: Classification of antiholomorphic involutions (real structures) on an elliptic curve via reflections of the lattice. Rectangular case is type E_a (two real ovals); rhombic case is type E'_a (one oval). The invariant is a = Q(e−)/Q(e+).
ideas.modern_name: Classification of real elliptic curves / real structures on complex tori
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein, Comessatti; modern treatments by Alling–Greenleaf and Silhol

ideas.what: a(−σ) = 1/a(σ), because −σ swaps the invariant and anti-invariant sublattices. Consequently σ and −σ are conjugate in G only in the square case.
ideas.modern_name: Number of non-isomorphic real forms of an elliptic curve; behaviour at j = 1728

ideas.what: Special lattices: square (E_1 and E'_1) and hexagonal (E'_{√3} and E'_{1/√3}).
ideas.modern_name: Real forms of the CM curves j = 1728 and j = 0

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, elementary rederivation of the classical classification of real structures on elliptic curves. It is a working step in the 1983–84 conformal-surgery notes. It contains a wrong guess about j and a possible factor slip (√3 versus 3). Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Section heading reads 'Distinguons les cas' rather than 'Reprenons [?] les cas'.
Marginal insertion: '(réflexion par rapport à l'orthogonale à celle de σ)', explaining what −σ is.
In the crossed-out line, 'j = (1/?) log a ?' is a tentative guess. In the image the crossed-out fragment reads 'ici a = exp j ou a = exp −j'.
